items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: I remember him. I remember him. ... Louie was driving a cold dump car.

ctx.x: And how many guys in the band? Do you remember the band that band? It was four then, at that time, I remember. What was your uncle playing?

He didn't even have no drum with him. He was playing Ghetto at that time. Uh-huh. He was taking up banjo in later years. That's when he went with Louis. He plays occasionally at, you know, like all weekends out there in California.

Well, guys like that, they aren't good enough to work. They only work with Louis Armstrong, Jelly Roll Morton, King Oliver, and all the rest of them. And yet today they're not working. Isn't that funny?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Is he on that one, Dr. Jazz? ... [INTERVIEWEE] You figure that's, yeah. Yeah. You know that guy, he had that mic.

ctx.x: And I had my belt and all. Oh yeah, you were sitting there. Because Nick had told us to bring them along with us, you know? Yeah. Yeah, I get you.

And still on these records, well, on this one, someone I'll be meaning to ask you. Where is it? Is he on that one, Dr. Jazz? Uh-huh. Well, you sing on that. Yeah. And on that, the drums is terribly seem to be over recorded, you know? They seem to be loud around the rest. Yeah, yeah it was.

You figure that's, yeah. Yeah. You know that guy, he had that mic. Mm-hmm. See, it's one of the tall mics, you know? Yeah. Because he was up on the stand. Yeah. And he had it protruding too close. Mm-hmm. Because see, I was right in the center. See, George, George and, uh, Howard and Jim was on this side of me. Yeah, that's on the right hand side. And, uh, Elton was on that side. Mm-hmm. And drag and drag was on this side of me. Right. On the left. See, well, naturally, he was picking up more volume with that…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: The interviewee mentions Louis Armstrong in the context of other musicians (Johnny Saint Seale, Joe Lindsey, Kid Ory) and historical settings, but never claims a direct personal interaction, collaboration, or meeting with Armstrong himself.

ctx.x: Yeah. I think it was a 28. And well I never did actually let me set in because I was kind of leery about setting in and you know in anybody's band or anything like that. So while we was living in Calton, Johnny Saint Seale was living up there at that time, well he used to play a little combo right at the corner from his house at Boydette and Hickory. He was living on Hickory between Boydette and Adams. Well he used to play there and he didn't have no drums handed so they had long benches and I used to have a pair…
Yes, he played with Faith Marable. Yeah, that's right, yeah, Faith Marable, yeah.
